human_tolerance.notes: Authored simulation estimate: the taxon is studied in urban Brazilian forest fragments, but this record does not claim garden visits or citywide thriving.

phases.name: mating
phases.note: Full-year neutral envelope because the source only relates mating to locally seasonal fruit and country-scale BR records do not establish a single breeding calendar; it does not assert continuous breeding.

taxonomy.note: GBIF species match returned canonical Nasua nasua, species rank, ACCEPTED, usage key 2433536; independently confirmed at iNaturalist taxon 41670, active species rank with no taxon changes.

conservation.note: Wikidata carries IUCN category Least Concern.

range.note: Country list follows the stated tropical and subtropical South American distribution; BR is native. GBIF and iNaturalist national occurrences independently support presence, not establishment status. Introduced and invasive Mallorca (ES) is included from the cited range source.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Coatis are terrestrial and climb and swim well. Climb remains listed as a biological locomotion mode, but the kit has no climbing action or pose. Swim is omitted because this quadruped plan's swim preview reproduces its walk pose, so the record cannot represent swimming distinctly.

traits.nest_type.note: Females give birth in tree nests; mapped to Platform.

traits.size_class.note: Medium follows the typical mass estimate and schema thresholds.

traits.mass_kg.note: 4.6 kg is the midpoint of the reported 2.0-7.2 kg mass range; this is a representative simulation estimate, not a published mean.

traits.length_m.note: 1.0 m is the midpoint of reported total length 0.85-1.13 m; includes tail.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 7.5 y is the midpoint of ADW's wild-lifespan estimate of about 7-8 y (Lifespan/Longevity, citing Nowak 1991 and Kasalinkas 1999). This is used as a typical-wild estimate, not as a maximum. NC is last resort: permissive alternatives checked were PanTHERIA/AnAge and the open Brazilian survival study Barreto et al. 2021; AnAge exposes captive maximum longevity, while Barreto et al. estimate annual apparent survival but not lifespan. Neither supports typical wild lifespan.

traits.diet.note: Authored model allocation: 0.4 invertebrate, 0.35 fruit, 0.2 small vertebrates, 0.05 carrion. Source supports these food categories and that fruits/invertebrates are prominent, but not their numeric proportions.

traits.social.note: Females and juveniles form bands of 15-30; adult males are usually solitary. The range models female/juvenile bands.

traits.defense.note: Flee response is a simulation mapping from descent and ground escape when disturbed.

traits.wariness.note: Authored judgement based on reports of entering human habitations; 0.65.

habitat.use.note: Authored ground/canopy split because animals are mostly terrestrial but climb and sleep in trees.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Resting and nesting in trees represented by shrub thicket shelter.

habitat.resources.note: Resource weights mirror the authored diet allocation, not measured frequencies.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Authored mapping to Adapter based on the existence of urban forest-fragment populations; it does not claim garden use or that urban populations thrive.

seasonal.note: Breeding is linked to locally seasonal fruit, but country-scale BR evidence does not establish a single calendar. The full-year mating window is a neutral schema-required envelope, not a claim of continuous breeding.

behavior.note: Species-local FSM provides reachable feeding actions for the modeled invertebrate, fruit, vertebrate, and carrion diet; walk is used for feeding, wandering, fleeing, and drinking. Night rest is represented through a sun-elevation gate. Climbing, swimming, and arboreal resting remain unsupported by the current behavior/action vocabulary; the look's swim pose was also removed because it rendered as walking.

look.note: Palette follows brown/rust coat, lighter underside, dark eye markings and ringed tail; proportions are authored to represent long snout and tail.

activity.BR.note: Empirical observation-frequency curve from BR country queries; monthly counts are not population abundance or proof of seasonal absence.
